question: Which verb correctly completes the sentence: 'A bouquet of red roses ___ on the table'? 🌹
explanation: Excellent! Even though 'roses' is plural, the actual subject of the sentence is 'A bouquet', which is a singular collective noun. Therefore, we use the singular verb 'is'! 🏺
hint: Look at the main subject word before the preposition 'of'.

question: Choose the correct verb: 'Bread and butter ___ my favorite breakfast.' 🍞
explanation: Brilliant! When two singular nouns joined by 'and' refer to the same idea or single item (like a single dish), they take a singular verb. 🧈
hint: Think of 'bread and butter' as one single meal.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Neither the teacher nor the students ___ in the classroom.' 🏫
explanation: Awesome! In a 'neither/nor' sentence, the verb must agree with the subject that is closest to it. Since 'students' is plural, we use 'are'. 📚
hint: Look at the noun right next to the blank!

question: Fill in the blank: 'The police ___ patrolling the streets tonight.' 🚓
explanation: Great job! The word 'police' is a noun that looks singular but is always treated as plural in English. 🚔
hint: Think of 'police' as a group of officers.

question: Which verb fits here: 'Mathematics ___ my favorite subject.' 📐
explanation: Perfect! Nouns that end in '-ics' like Mathematics, Physics, and Gymnastics are singular, even though they end in 's'. 🧮
hint: It is the name of ONE single subject.

question: Choose the correct option: 'Each of the girls ___ given a certificate.' 📜
explanation: Fantastic! The pronoun 'Each' is always singular. Even though it is followed by 'of the girls', the main subject is 'Each'. 🏅
hint: Focus on the first word of the sentence.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The team ___ practicing hard for the finals.' ⚽
explanation: Super! 'Team' is a collective noun. Since they are acting together as a single unit, we use a singular verb. ⛹️
hint: They are doing the action together as one group.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Either my sister or my brothers ___ going to the store.' 🛒
explanation: Excellent! When using 'either/or', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. 'Brothers' is plural, so the verb is 'are'. 🍇
hint: Check the subject right next to the verb.

question: Which verb is correct: 'Ten kilometers ___ a long distance to walk.' 🚶‍♂️
explanation: Brilliant! Distances, periods of time, and sums of money are treated as singular units when considered as a whole. 👟
hint: Think of it as one single continuous distance.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The news on TV tonight ___ very interesting.' 📺
explanation: Awesome! The word 'news' ends in 's', but it is an uncountable, singular noun. 🎙️
hint: It is a single broadcast or report.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Everyone in the room ___ cheering loudly.' 🎉
explanation: Great! Indefinite pronouns like everyone, everybody, someone, and nobody always take singular verbs. 🥳
hint: Words ending in '-one' or '-body' are singular.

question: Choose the right verb: 'A pair of scissors ___ on the desk.' ✂️
explanation: Perfect! While 'scissors' alone is plural, the phrase 'A pair of' acts as a singular subject. 📏
hint: Look at the words 'A pair'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The principal, along with the teachers, ___ attending the meeting.' 👔
explanation: Fantastic! Phrases like 'along with', 'as well as', and 'besides' do not change the number of the subject. The verb agrees with the first subject, 'The principal'. 🏫
hint: Ignore the phrase set off by commas and match the verb to the first noun.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Both of my dogs ___ collars.' 🐕
explanation: Super! The word 'Both' implies two, so it is a plural subject and requires a plural verb. 🐾
hint: Does 'Both' refer to one or more than one?

question: Which verb is correct: 'The jury ___ divided in their opinions.' ⚖️
explanation: Excellent! Collective nouns take a plural verb when the members are acting individually or are divided. 🧑‍⚖️
hint: Are they acting as one unit, or disagreeing as individuals?

question: Choose the correct option: 'Slow and steady ___ the race.' 🐢
explanation: Brilliant! 'Slow and steady' expresses a single idea or quality, so it takes a singular verb. 🥇
hint: Think of it as a single famous proverb or concept.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Many a student ___ made this mistake before.' 🎒
explanation: Awesome! The phrase 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and always takes a singular verb. 📝
hint: Focus on the 'a' right before 'student'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Two-thirds of the pie ___ eaten.' 🥧
explanation: Great job! For fractions, the verb agrees with the noun after 'of'. Since 'pie' is singular and uncountable, the verb is singular. 🥄
hint: Look at the word after 'of'.

question: Which verb fits here: 'A number of students ___ waiting outside.' 🚪
explanation: Perfect! The phrase 'A number of' means 'several' or 'many' and always takes a plural verb. 👥
hint: 'A number of' means 'many'.

question: Choose the right verb: 'The number of students in the class ___ thirty.' 📊
explanation: Fantastic! Unlike 'a number of', the phrase 'The number of' refers to a specific, singular quantity, so it takes a singular verb. 📈
hint: It refers to one specific total count.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Either you or he ___ to apologize.' 🤝
explanation: Super! In an 'either/or' sentence, match the verb to the subject closest to it. 'He' is singular, so use 'has'. 🫂
hint: Look at the pronoun right next to the blank.

question: Fill in the blank: 'None of the garbage ___ been picked up.' 🗑️
explanation: Excellent! 'None' can be singular or plural depending on the noun after it. 'Garbage' is uncountable (singular), so the verb is singular. 🚮
hint: Is 'garbage' countable or uncountable?

question: Which verb is correct: 'Not only the teacher but also the students ___ excited.' 😃
explanation: Brilliant! With 'Not only... but also', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Students' is plural! 🎒
hint: Look at the word right after 'but also'.

question: Choose the correct option: 'Measles ___ a contagious disease.' 🤒
explanation: Awesome! The names of certain diseases, like measles or mumps, end in 's' but are treated as singular. 🛏️
hint: It is the name of one specific illness.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The cattle ___ grazing in the field.' 🐄
explanation: Great! 'Cattle' is a plural noun, even though it doesn't end in 's'. It refers to many cows. 🚜
hint: This word describes a large group of animals.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Fifty dollars ___ too much for that shirt.' 👕
explanation: Perfect! Sums of money are treated as a single, collective amount, so they take a singular verb. 💵
hint: Think of it as one total price.

question: Which verb fits here: 'The writer and poet ___ arriving today.' ✍️
explanation: Fantastic! Because there is only one article ('The') before 'writer', it means the writer and poet are the same person. So, the verb is singular! 🖋️
hint: Count how many times the word 'The' appears before the nouns.

question: Choose the right verb: 'The writer and the poet ___ arriving today.' 🎭
explanation: Super! Here, the article 'the' is repeated before both nouns, meaning they are two different people. Therefore, the verb is plural. 🤝
hint: Look closely at the word 'the' before 'poet'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Every boy and girl ___ to participate.' 🙋‍♀️
explanation: Excellent! When subjects are preceded by 'Every', the verb is always singular, even if there are multiple subjects connected by 'and'. 🤸
hint: The word 'Every' forces the verb to be singular.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Nobody ___ the trouble I've seen.' 👀
explanation: Brilliant! 'Nobody' is an indefinite pronoun, and it always requires a singular verb. 🧠
hint: Think of 'Nobody' as 'not a single person'.

question: Which verb is correct: 'The herd of elephants ___ moving towards the river.' 🐘
explanation: Awesome! 'Herd' is a collective noun acting as a single, unified group, so it takes a singular verb. 🌿
hint: Focus on the word 'herd', not 'elephants'.

question: Choose the correct option: 'My friend and guide ___ helped me a lot.' 🌟
explanation: Great job! Because 'friend' and 'guide' refer to the exact same person, we use a singular verb. 🧭
hint: Is this one person acting in two roles, or two different people?

question: Complete the sentence: 'A lot of the apples ___ rotten.' 🍎
explanation: Perfect! With terms like 'A lot of', you look at the noun that follows. 'Apples' is plural, so the verb is plural! 🐛
hint: Look at the noun after 'of'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'A lot of the water ___ spilled.' 💧
explanation: Fantastic! Here, 'water' follows 'a lot of'. Since 'water' is uncountable (singular), the verb must be singular. 🚰
hint: Can you count water? If not, it's singular.

question: Which verb fits here: 'The boy, along with his parents, ___ going to the zoo.' 🦁
explanation: Super! Phrases like 'along with' do not make a compound subject. The true subject is 'The boy', which is singular. 🐒
hint: Ignore the words trapped between the commas.

question: Choose the right verb: 'Neither of the cars ___ working.' 🚗
explanation: Excellent! The pronoun 'Neither' acts as a singular subject, meaning 'not one or the other'. So it takes a singular verb. 🛠️
hint: The subject is 'Neither', not 'cars'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Fire and water ___ not mix.' 🔥
explanation: Brilliant! Fire and water are two entirely different and distinct things joined by 'and', so they form a plural subject. 🧊
hint: Are they two separate elements?

question: Fill in the blank: 'Someone ___ left their bag here.' 🎒
explanation: Awesome! 'Someone' is an indefinite pronoun, and it always takes a singular verb. 🏫
hint: Think of 'Someone' as one mystery person.

question: Which verb is correct: 'The committee ___ agreed on the new rules.' 📝
explanation: Great! When a collective noun like 'committee' acts together as a single unit with one mind, it takes a singular verb. ✍️
hint: They agreed together as one group.

question: Choose the correct option: 'Five miles ___ a long way to run.' 🏃
explanation: Perfect! Distances are treated as one continuous stretch, so they require a singular verb. 🏁
hint: Treat it as one total distance.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Those trousers ___ too long for you.' 👖
explanation: Fantastic! Nouns that refer to items with two equal parts (trousers, scissors, glasses) are always plural. 👞
hint: Trousers have two legs!

question: Fill in the blank: 'Gulliver’s Travels ___ a fascinating book.' 📖
explanation: Super! Even though the title ends in an 's', it is the name of ONE single book. 📚
hint: It is just one title.

question: Which verb fits here: 'Either the cats or the dog ___ responsible for the mess.' 🐶
explanation: Excellent! In an 'either/or' sentence, look at the noun closest to the verb. 'Dog' is singular, so the verb is 'is'. 🗑️
hint: Which animal is closest to the blank?

question: Choose the right verb: 'Neither the dogs nor the cat ___ responsible for the mess.' 🐱
explanation: Brilliant! Just like 'either/or', in 'neither/nor', the verb matches the closest subject. 'Cat' is singular! 🧶
hint: Which noun is closer to the verb?

question: Complete the sentence: 'Half of the students ___ passed the test.' 🎓
explanation: Awesome! When using fractions like 'Half of', look at the noun. 'Students' is plural, so we use the plural verb 'have'. 💯
hint: Look at the noun after 'of'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Rice and curry ___ a popular dish in India.' 🍛
explanation: Great job! Just like 'bread and butter', 'rice and curry' represents one single dish or meal, so it takes a singular verb. 🥘
hint: They are eaten together as one item.

question: Which verb is correct: 'The scissors ___ in the top drawer.' ✂️
explanation: Perfect! 'Scissors' is a plural noun because it represents a tool with two blades. It needs a plural verb unless preceded by 'a pair of'. 🗄️
hint: It has two blades, so it acts like a plural word.

question: Choose the correct option: 'Time and tide ___ for no man.' 🌊
explanation: Fantastic! This is a famous proverb where 'Time' and 'Tide' are treated as two distinct forces, requiring a plural verb. ⏳
hint: Are time and tide the same thing, or two different things?

question: Complete the sentence: 'A pack of wolves ___ howling at the moon.' 🐺
explanation: Super! 'A pack' is a singular collective noun. Even though there are many wolves, there is only one pack! 🌕
hint: Look at the word 'pack', not 'wolves'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Nothing ___ impossible if you believe.' 🌟
explanation: Excellent! 'Nothing' is a singular indefinite pronoun, so it always takes a singular verb! Keep believing! 🚀
hint: Indefinite pronouns with '-thing' are always singular.
